task_spec: SUBJECT: A new route/tab in traktor-nml-tool's NiceGUI wizard app (C:\codex\traktor-nml-tool) letting an operator build an NML playlist from a base collection plus a supplied Artist/Title tracklist, matched via the existing matching cascade, entirely through the GUI rather than only the CLI's build-playlist subcommand.

SCOPE: traktor_nml/gui/ (app.py, navigation.py, theme.py, a new build-playlist view module), traktor_nml/buildplaylist.py and traktor_nml/tracklist.py as the core logic driven (not duplicated), design/reconnect-wizard/ (a new artboard, if this plan's first milestone determines one is needed), traktor_nml/README.md decision log (DL-260 onward), docs/plans/ (new dated plan directory)

OUT-OF-SCOPE: keyboard-navigation, focus-ring, tab-order, screen-reader/announcement work beyond whatever the existing header-tab shell and theme.py already give for free (standing user preference, no new accessibility milestone); editing anything in the sibling C:\codex\traktor-nml-tool-plan repository (frozen archival, tag plan-final-w004, takes no new plans); changing build_playlist_cmd.py's CLI behavior, exit codes or output bytes (constraint precedent: prior GUI-adjacent plans keep CLI output byte-identical); building a full review/conflict-resolution UI for ambiguous/unmatched tracklist lines beyond a first pass (flag as a possible follow-on milestone, not assumed in scope)
constraints: MUST: reuse traktor_nml/buildplaylist.py's assemble_output and traktor_nml/tracklist.py's parse_tracklist/resolve_tracklist as the core the GUI drives - do not reimplement matching, resolution or NML node synthesis in gui/ (precedent: app.py drives run_reconnection/write_reconnect_result today rather than reimplementing reconnect logic)
MUST NOT: change traktor_nml/commands/build_playlist_cmd.py's CLI behavior, stdout/stderr/exit-code contract, or written output bytes - this is GUI-only work

MUST: any new nicegui-free logic (e.g. a view-model layer analogous to review_model.py/wizard_state.py) imports no nicegui/pywebview, so the system pytest interpreter (no nicegui installed) can guard it directly - established package convention (see gui/CLAUDE.md's nicegui boundary, DL-069)

MUST: the new route follows the existing header-tab mechanism from docs/plans/2026-09-03-header-tabs (DL-129..DL-147) exactly - an anchor per route in navigation.py's tab table, aria-current="page" plus wizard-tab-selected on the active tab, equality comparison against exactly one route, never membership - rather than inventing a new nav pattern
MUST NOT: schedule a keyboard-contract or announcements/accessibility milestone for this new screen (standing user preference; out of scope until the user explicitly asks)

MUST: new decision log entries are appended starting at DL-260. traktor_nml/README.md is the authority for the high-water mark and states it as DL-259, the tail of the implemented docs/plans/2026-09-15-resolve-detail-rail block. An unimplemented block yields to an implemented one and shifts whole, per docs/2026-08-26-renderer-split-plan.md:92 and docs/plans/2026-09-03-header-tabs/README.md:24 - re-read the live mark immediately before minting new DL numbers, since this file is a point-in-time snapshot and more same-day work may land after it was written

SHOULD: if design/reconnect-wizard/Specs.dc.html or a new artboard is the design of record for this screen (DL-071's precedent: Specs governs what the operator sees and presses), determine in an early milestone whether a wireframe must be drafted before UI requirements are written, rather than inventing UI details unmoored from a design source
entry_points: traktor_nml/commands/build_playlist_cmd.py:_handle_build_playlist - the CLI's whole surface: path-collision refusal (output vs base/tracklist, unresolved-report vs all three), reading+decoding the tracklist (utf-8-sig BOM strip), calling assemble_output, printing stats, writing the unresolved-report CSV, the --full-collection isolation pass via split.py's build_output, atomic write. The GUI's write path should mirror this command's sequencing and refusals.

traktor_nml/buildplaylist.py - core module: UnresolvedRow/BuildPlaylistResult dataclasses, assemble_output(base_bytes, base_root, tracklist_text, name, target_folder, allow_unmatched) - resolves lines via tracklist.py's resolve_tracklist at MatchConfidence.LOOSE, synthesizes a NODE TYPE=PLAYLIST via playlists.synthesize_playlist_node, inserts via spans.py byte-span assembly (OutputBuilder/SpanIndex/find_element_span). No source span exists for a playlist built from external text, so it always takes the ElementTree-serialization path (DL-028) rather than transplantation.
traktor_nml/tracklist.py - parse_tracklist (parses 'Artist - Title' lines), resolve_tracklist (per-line matched/unmatched/ambiguous resolution against a base collection's EntryRecords)

traktor_nml/gui/app.py - the existing wizard's page-building/wiring layer; the new build-playlist view should follow its pattern of driving core logic under nicegui.run.io_bound and feeding ui.log/ui.state from render functions, without holding matching or assembly logic itself
traktor_nml/gui/navigation.py - the framework-free tab table + selection-rule module from the header-tabs plan (DL-129..DL-147); the new route is a third entry here

traktor_nml/gui/theme.py - Specs' token module (colors/type/spacing/radii, page_stylesheet()); the new screen's classes, if any beyond what theme.py already defines, extend this module rather than hardcoding values in app.py

traktor_nml/gui/review_model.py and wizard_state.py - the closest existing precedent for a nicegui-free per-record decision/status model (six Specs statuses, filter chips, decision state); a build-playlist review layer (for unmatched/ambiguous tracklist lines) would likely follow this same shape rather than a new one

When it arrives it is its own entry point, not a branch of this one.' This is the design-of-record's own statement that this screen needs its own artboard, not a graft onto the reconnect wizard's Specs.

Duplicating buildplaylist.py's/tracklist.py's resolution and assembly logic inside gui/ - rejected per the package's established layering (every write command pairs a core module with a thin surface: splice.py/splice_cmd.py, split.py/split_cmd.py, buildplaylist.py/build_playlist_cmd.py; the GUI should be a third thin surface over the same core, per how app.py already drives reconnect's core rather than reimplementing it)

Inventing a new navigation/tab mechanism for the third route - rejected in favor of extending navigation.py's existing tab table (DL-129..DL-147), since the header-tabs plan already settled the mechanism (anchor+aria-current, equality-only comparison) after enumerating pitfalls

Scheduling keyboard/focus-ring/accessibility work for this new screen now - explicitly out of scope per standing user preference; the reconnect wizard's own such work is done (already shipped, per the frozen plan-tool repo) but this new screen does not inherit an obligation to redo that work immediately
current_understanding: traktor-nml-tool is a CLI+GUI package for repairing/rebuilding Traktor NML collection and playlist files. The GUI is a NiceGUI app with a header-tab shell: '/' serves a 'reconstruct' page (rebuilding playlists deleted from a collection, via splice --reconstruct-playlists), '/reconnect' serves the reconnect wizard (repointing collection entries whose files moved). Both routes share one header with a brand mark and a tab strip (navigation.py + theme.py), established by docs/plans/2026-09-03-header-tabs.

build-playlist is a third, semantically distinct operation, already fully implemented as a CLI-only subcommand: given a base NML collection and a plain-text tracklist of 'Artist - Title' lines, it matches each line against the collection (via the shared matching cascade at a fixed LOOSE confidence, since a text-only line has no path/size/time to match on more strictly) and writes a brand-new NML playlist file containing the matched entries in input order. It handles output/input path collisions, an optional --target-folder, --full-collection vs isolated single-playlist output, --allow-unmatched, an --unresolved-report CSV, and --dry-run. None of this is exposed in the GUI today.

The package's planning scheme changed over time: early large plans (like the reconnect wizard's) lived in a dedicated sibling repo (traktor-nml-tool-plan) with full replay/verification machinery (plan.json + code_changes + byte-identical replay against real commits). That repo is now frozen (tag plan-final-w004) and explicitly takes no new plans. The current, lighter scheme is one dated directory per plan under traktor-nml-tool/docs/plans/, with no code_changes/replay machinery, the newest of which (2026-08-29-playlist-reconstruction onward) already uses this lighter form.

The most recently completed plan is docs/plans/2026-09-07-reconstruct-resolve-step (all three milestones committed and closed, DL-198..DL-215, browser record at docs/2026-09-07-reconstruct-resolve-browser-record.md). Its README notes it 'carries a README.md recording the three defects that run found and the keyboard ring it could not walk' - i.e. even the most recent completed GUI plan explicitly declined to complete a keyboard-ring reading for schedule reasons, consistent with the user's standing preference to keep that class of work out of scope unless asked for.
assumptions: That the GUI should offer a first pass at handling unmatched/ambiguous tracklist lines (some minimal review surface), rather than only a happy-path form-and-write screen with allow-unmatched/dry-run toggles (M). The planner should confirm scope for this with an early milestone/decision rather than assuming a full review UI is needed on day one.

That DL-259 is still README.md's current high-water mark by the time this plan actually mints new entries (M) - same-day work lands on this package without a docs/plans/ directory of its own; re-check immediately before writing DL-260 onward.

That a new artboard is warranted before writing GUI requirements, per Specs.dc.html's own statement that build-playlist 'has its own review model' and 'is its own entry point' (H, directly stated by the design of record) - but the planner should still treat 'draft the artboard first' as an explicit milestone decision to confirm, not silently skip.

That the base collection and the tracklist are both supplied as file paths (matching the CLI's `base`/`tracklist` positional args) rather than the GUI needing e.g. a paste-in-text tracklist entry (M) - worth confirming against how the reconnect wizard currently gathers its own file inputs (native file picker via file_picker.py) for consistency.
invisible_knowledge: DL-071 (reconnect wizard): Specs.dc.html/an artboard is the design of record - it governs what the operator sees and presses; a Specs-vs-code disagreement is recorded rather than silently resolved. Any new screen should get the same treatment: a named artboard, or an explicit decision that none exists yet and requirements are provisional pending one.

DL-028 (buildplaylist.py): a playlist built from external tracklist text has no source span in the base NML, so its fragment always takes the ElementTree-serialization path rather than transplantation - relevant if the GUI needs to preview the fragment before writing.

The package's nicegui-boundary convention (DL-069 and reaffirmed across every GUI plan since): everything reducible to data/arithmetic - status derivation, decision state, filter predicates, token tables, tab selection - lives in a module that imports no nicegui, so the system pytest interpreter (which has no nicegui installed) can guard it directly; app.py itself is left holding wiring only and is comparatively untested, so milestones buy their confidence for app.py's own wiring through a served-page browser-record gate written to docs/, not through pytest alone.

The reconnect-wizard's own keyboard/accessibility work (equivalent milestones in the now-frozen plan-tool repo) already shipped - traktor_nml/gui/keymap.py, announce.py and theme.py's accessibility tokens exist and are built. That does not obligate this new screen to replicate that work immediately; the user has stated keyboard/accessibility work is out of scope for new work until they say otherwise.

Every existing write command in this package pairs a thin commands/ CLI surface with a core module holding the real logic (splice.py/splice_cmd.py, split.py/split_cmd.py, buildplaylist.py/build_playlist_cmd.py) - the GUI is naturally a second thin surface over the same core modules, following the same layering rather than becoming a third place logic can drift.
